measurements.title: Heart rate
measurements.method: Approved monitor or an existing demo value
measurements.why: Heart rate adds cardiovascular context, but recent exercise, measurement conditions, and individual patterns matter.
measurements.limit: This app does not acquire a pulse, validate a sensor, or establish an emergency diagnosis.

steps.title: Confirm the person and purpose
steps.text: Check the selected crew member and whether the value represents rest, exercise, or another documented context.

steps.title: Follow the instrument's instructions
steps.text: In real operations, use the approved monitor, placement instructions, and mission procedure. This illustration is not a sensor-placement guide.

steps.title: Read the value and unit
steps.text: Use the displayed beats-per-minute value. Record instrument warnings or uncertain measurement conditions rather than assuming a valid result.

steps.title: Record and read back
steps.text: For this demonstration, enter a fictional bpm value, add context in notes, and review the crew and measurement before confirming.

measurements.title: Blood pressure
measurements.method: Approved pressure monitor or a fictional pair
measurements.why: Systolic and diastolic values provide cardiovascular context when measured consistently and interpreted appropriately.
measurements.limit: Earth-based positioning advice cannot simply be assumed to apply in microgravity. This app does not select cuff size, calibrate equipment, or provide medical thresholds.

steps.title: Check the crew and equipment
steps.text: In real use, confirm the instrument, cuff, units, and approved procedure. Do not derive equipment instructions from this demo.

steps.title: Document measurement conditions
steps.text: Use the mission-approved positioning and measurement conditions for the actual environment. Note recent activity or other relevant context.

steps.title: Distinguish the two numbers
steps.text: Record systolic and diastolic separately in mmHg. The form checks that systolic is greater than diastolic as a data-consistency check only.

steps.title: Review the pair
steps.text: Enter fictional values into the two labeled inputs. Verify that neither the numbers nor the units have been swapped before recording.

measurements.title: Sleep duration
measurements.method: Self-report, sleep log, or a recorded device summary
measurements.why: Sleep supports alertness and recovery. Light cycles, noise, schedules, isolation, and workload can affect the sleep experience.
measurements.limit: Duration alone does not diagnose a sleep condition or establish readiness for a task.

steps.title: Choose a consistent sleep period
steps.text: Use the same reporting convention from one check-in to the next, following the actual mission routine where applicable.

steps.title: Use a recorded total
steps.text: Refer to your log or device summary. Do not enter the current clock time or a planned sleep duration as though it were completed sleep.

steps.title: Keep the units clear
steps.text: The field uses decimal hours: for example, 6.5 hours represents six and a half hours. Note interruptions or uncertainty.

steps.title: Enter and review
steps.text: Use a fictional total for this demo. Compare it with the synthetic personal pattern, alongside workload and self-reported fatigue.

measurements.title: Fatigue check-in
measurements.why: A consistent self-report can add useful context to sleep and operational workload.
measurements.limit: The app's 1–5 scale is a demo convention, not a validated clinical or fitness-for-duty test.

steps.title: Pause and consider the context
steps.text: Think about perceived effort, recent rest, and workload. The app does not measure fatigue automatically.

steps.title: Read the scale
steps.text: The demo labels run from 1, very low fatigue, to 5, very high fatigue. They are not medical severity categories.

steps.title: Choose consistently
steps.text: Use the same interpretation on repeated entries. Add a note if an unusual task or interruption helps explain the value.

steps.title: Review with sleep
steps.text: Record the fictional self-report, then review it alongside the sleep and activity context rather than treating it as a diagnosis.

measurements.title: Mood check-in
measurements.why: A simple check-in creates space to notice and communicate well-being changes during isolation and confinement.
measurements.limit: The choices are not a mental-health screening instrument. This prototype does not evaluate or manage a crisis.

steps.title: Use the intended reporting period
steps.text: Consider how the fictional crew member is feeling for this check-in, not a diagnosis or personality label.

steps.title: Choose a description
steps.text: Select Low, Fair, Good, or Great as a demonstration self-report. There is no automatic inference from a face, camera, or other signal.

steps.title: Add helpful context
steps.text: Optional notes can explain the demo situation. Do not enter real sensitive or identifying information into this public prototype.

steps.title: Review and communicate appropriately
steps.text: Confirm the entry. For real concerns, follow the established mission support and care procedures rather than relying on this demo.

measurements.title: Exercise & effort
measurements.why: Activity records connect movement with sleep, perceived effort, and recovery context during spaceflight.
measurements.limit: The catalog's example duration is not a prescription. No calories, exercise safety, or overtraining diagnosis is calculated.

steps.title: Identify the activity
steps.text: Choose the matching demo activity. In real operations, use only mission-approved equipment, setup, and protocols.

steps.title: Record completed time
steps.text: Enter the completed minutes, not the planned time. Edit the auto-filled example duration if it does not match the fictional session.

steps.title: Describe effort and context
steps.text: Use the labeled 1–10 demo effort scale, where 1 is very light and 10 extremely hard. Add relevant interruptions or equipment context.

steps.title: Review the session
steps.text: Check the crew, activity, duration, and effort before confirming. Review sleep and fatigue context without assuming that the app has cleared exercise as safe.

hazards.title: Space radiation
hazards.context: Radiation exposure is a distinct spaceflight hazard.
hazards.limit: Heart rate, mood, and blood pressure do not measure radiation dose. No dosimetry is connected.

hazards.title: Isolation & confinement
hazards.context: Sleep, workload, communication, and well-being can be relevant to the crew experience.
hazards.limit: Self-reports do not diagnose a behavioral-health condition.

hazards.title: Distance from Earth
hazards.context: Communications and available support can differ by mission environment.
hazards.limit: This demo does not implement medical communications, emergency procedures, or a verified offline library.

hazards.title: Gravity fields
hazards.context: Different gravity environments change adaptation, equipment needs, and measurement context.
hazards.limit: Choosing a scenario does not provide evidence for changing thresholds or scaling baseline values.

hazards.title: Hostile closed environments
hazards.context: A confined habitat introduces environmental and operational considerations.
hazards.limit: This app does not measure cabin air quality or infer habitat safety from crew readings.

contexts.title: Orbital station
contexts.description: An example orbital setting, consistent with the fictional source mission. Consider scheduled routines, equipment setup, sleep conditions, and activity context.
contexts.measurementNote: Use the approved orbital equipment and positioning instructions; ordinary Earth measurement setups are not automatically transferable.

contexts.title: Deep-space transit
contexts.communications: Delayed or unavailable contact may occur
contexts.description: A scenario preview emphasizing distance, isolation, and access to approved information when immediate ground contact is not available.
contexts.measurementNote: Measurement and response procedures must be mission-approved. This demo does not replace autonomous medical training or provide a verified offline protocol.

contexts.title: Lunar surface
contexts.communications: Availability depends on the actual mission
contexts.description: A scenario preview emphasizing surface operations, altered loading, equipment constraints, and environmental context.
contexts.measurementNote: Do not rescale the displayed physiological baselines based only on gravity. Relevant procedures and evidence must be evaluated separately.

contexts.title: Mars surface
contexts.description: A scenario preview emphasizing long-duration habitation, isolation, equipment availability, and clear records for later review.
contexts.measurementNote: The source measurements remain fictional orbital records. This preview changes educational explanations only, not nominal ranges or diagnostic rules.

routines.title: Record a demo health check-in
routines.description: Review the selected crew member and enter fictional measurements.

routines.title: Review movement & log a demo session
routines.description: Record completed activity, duration, and perceived effort.

routines.title: Review measurement limits & sources
routines.description: Read the walkthrough and source limitations, then mark this self-review complete.
